exercises.title: Roger

exercises.note: Careful: Roger does NOT mean "yes". It only confirms you heard the message.

units.title: Unit 3 · Aviation Numbers
units.subtitle: The special radio pronunciation of numbers

exercises.title: Why are numbers pronounced differently?
exercises.subtitle: Some numbers sound alike over the radio, so they're pronounced differently:
exercises.note: "Five" and "nine" can get lost in static, so they're said as "fife" and "niner".

exercises.prompt: How is the number 3 said on the radio?
How do you say the number 9 on the radio?
How is the number 5 said on the radio?
Match the numbers with their pronunciations

exercises.title: Numbers are read digit by digit
exercises.subtitle: Headings and altitudes are never read as a whole number — each digit is said on its own:
exercises.note: This is why 3, 5, and 9 have their own special pronunciation — you'll hear them constantly in headings and altitudes.

exercises.prompt: How do you read heading 090 on the radio?
How do you read flight level 350?
Read heading 270 in order
Match the heading with its spoken form

units.title: Unit 4 · Taxi, Takeoff & Landing Clearances
units.subtitle: The phraseology used to move on the ground and fly the pattern

exercises.title: Getting to the runway
exercises.subtitle: Key words for ground movement:

items.v: Move the aircraft on the ground under its own power
The point before the runway where you wait for clearance
Enter the runway and hold position
Permission to move on the ground to the runway

exercises.note: You must stop at the holding point until you're cleared to enter the runway.

exercises.prompt: What does "cleared to taxi" mean?
options: Permission to move on the ground to the runway

exercises.prompt: What is a Holding point?
options: The point before the runway where you wait for clearance

exercises.prompt: Match
Build the instruction: proceed to wait before the runway

options: Move the aircraft on the ground
The point before the runway where you wait
Permission to move on the ground

exercises.title: From the runway into the air
exercises.subtitle: Key words for takeoff:

items.v: Permission to begin the takeoff roll
Enter the runway, hold position, do not take off yet
The code you set on your transponder
The frequency to contact after takeoff

exercises.prompt: What does "Line up and wait" mean?
options: Enter the runway and take off immediately
Enter the runway and hold position, don't take off yet

exercises.prompt: What is a Squawk code?
options: A code you set on your transponder

exercises.prompt: Match
What do you call permission to begin the takeoff roll?

options: Permission to begin the takeoff roll
The code you set on your transponder
The frequency to contact after takeoff

exercises.title: Coming back down
exercises.subtitle: Key words for landing:

items.v: Abandon the approach and climb away
Repeating a clearance back to ATC to confirm it
The last, straight segment of the approach before landing

exercises.note: Readback isn't optional for important clearances — ATC needs to hear you got it right.

exercises.prompt: What does "Go around" mean?
options: Abandon the approach and climb away

exercises.prompt: Why do pilots do a Readback?
options: To confirm they received the clearance correctly

exercises.prompt: Match
Build the clearance: permission to land on runway two seven

options: Abandon the approach and climb away
Repeating a clearance back to ATC
The last segment of the approach

units.title: Unit 5 · Emergency & Urgency Phraseology
units.subtitle: How to declare and describe an emergency on the radio

exercises.title: Two levels of urgency
exercises.subtitle: Both are said three times in a row, but they mean different things:

items.v: Grave and imminent danger — a distress call
An urgent situation, but not immediate danger to life

exercises.note: Mayday, Mayday, Mayday — Pan-Pan, Pan-Pan, Pan-Pan. Always three times.

exercises.prompt: When do you say "Mayday"?
How many times is Mayday said in a row?
What does Pan-Pan indicate?
options: Urgency, but not immediate danger to life

exercises.prompt: Match

options: An urgent situation, but not immediate danger

exercises.title: What ATC needs to know
exercises.subtitle: After Mayday or Pan-Pan, give this information:

items.v: Total number of people on the aircraft
How much fuel is left, usually in time
What kind of problem you have
Asking to land before other traffic

exercises.prompt: What does "souls on board" mean?
options: Total number of people on the aircraft

exercises.prompt: Why state fuel remaining in an emergency?
options: So ATC knows how much time you have

exercises.prompt: Match
What do you call the total number of people on board?

options: Total number of people on the aircraft
What kind of problem you have
